meetings.title: Client delivery call — Northgate
meetings.summary: Delivery date moved to the 14th; the 12th is not achievable. Installation starts at 07:00 with full building access. Written confirmation before 17:00, training date to be confirmed. The client flagged Saturday overtime internally.

utterances.text: Recording is on. Everyone has been told this is for the project record — Sandra, Tomás, you're both fine with that?
Fine by me. Let's keep it to the delivery question; I have another call at half past.
I'll share the schedule so we're all looking at the same thing.
Good. The question from the client this morning was whether we can still make the 12th.
Right. The install crew is the constraint, not the hardware.
The crew finishes the Bracknell job on the 10th. After that we have two vans free.
And the building access? We only have the loading bay from seven until ten.
That's workable if we start on the Tuesday. It is not workable on the Thursday.
So the 12th is Thursday.
Correct. And the 14th is Saturday — quieter building, full access.
Saturday costs us overtime for our own team. I need to flag that internally.
Understood. Let's be explicit about the trade-off, then.
Let's walk the scope first, so the date decision is grounded.
Three parts: hardware delivery, installation, and the two-hour training.
Hardware is already in the warehouse. That is not the risk.
The risk is our access window and the lift booking.
The lift is booked for the Tuesday and the Saturday. Not the Thursday.
Okay. So if we say the 12th, we are promising a day the building cannot support.
That is how I read it.
I would rather move the date than run a half-install.
Agreed. Nobody wants a half-install.
The hardware is fine. The crew is fine. The building is the constraint.
And the crew needs a clear twelve-hour window. Two vans, four people.
On the Saturday we can give you seven until seven.
That works. On the Thursday we would lose the afternoon to the school run.
Let's put the access question in writing as well.
I'll add it to the confirmation.
Now the training. Is that the same visit or a separate one?
It was quoted as a separate visit, but we can fold it into the Saturday if the room is free.
The room is free on the Saturday. The trainer is not.
Our trainer is on another site that week.
So the 14th can include installation but not training, unless we move the trainer.
That is my understanding.
Let's not create a promise we cannot keep on training.
Agreed. Installation on the 14th, training to be confirmed separately.
If training is separate, I need one more van on the 17th.
Noted. I'll check availability and come back tomorrow.
And who covers the Saturday overtime for our team?
That is a commercial question. I'll take it offline with Sandra.
Thank you. I don't want my team out of pocket.
Fair.
Let's look at the support window next.
Thirty days from handover, remote first, one site visit included.
Does the thirty days start on the 14th or on the training day?
On handover. The 14th.
Then if training slips, our support is already running.
That's a fair point. We should align those dates.
I can start support on the training day instead. It is a small change.
That would be cleaner.
Let's note it as a proposed change, not agreed yet.
Proposed. I'll confirm with finance.
While we're on dates — the Bracknell job could slip by a day.
How likely is that?
Twenty percent. If it slips, the 14th is still safe. The 12th is not.
That reinforces the recommendation.
Then I think we should stop pretending the 12th is possible.
I agree. Let's make that the decision.
For the record: the 12th is not achievable with the current access and crew.
And the 14th is achievable if we confirm by Friday.
Confirm by Friday. Understood.
I'll hold the crew for the 14th until Friday noon.
Please do. We don't want to lose the slot.
Now the internal bit before we close.
Should I drop off for that?
No, stay — it's only scheduling.
Between us, Sandra's team is chaotic — they will not have the access list ready by the 12th anyway.
I heard that.
I'm sorry, that was unhelpful. Let me rephrase: the access list is the critical path.
Let's keep it factual. Access list owner and date.
I'll own it. Tuesday the 27th, end of day.
That gives us time to plan the vans.
Good. Tuesday the 27th.
I'll put that in the note.
And I'll copy my facilities lead.
Let's go back to the client-facing summary.
We need one sentence the client can forward internally.
Something like: installation moves to the 14th, access confirmed, training to follow.
That is accurate.
And the crew is held until Friday.
Good.
Now the commercial framing. The client asked whether the move costs them anything.
The install itself does not. The Saturday overtime is their side.
And our overtime is ours to absorb. I've already flagged it.
So we are not asking for more money.
Not for installation. Training is separate.
If training moves, that is a change order.
Understood. I'll say that plainly.
Do we need legal to review the confirmation?
No, it's an operational note. But keep the change-order language out of it.
Agreed.
One more thing — the loading bay has a 900 kilo lift limit.
The racks are 780. We're fine.
Fine on paper. I'll measure on the day.
Good. Any other risks?
Parking for the vans. Saturday is better, but we need two permits.
I'll add permits to the confirmation.
So the action list is growing. Let's capture it.
Confirmation, permits, schedule, crew hold.
And training date.
And the 17th van if training is separate.
On delivery: we can hold the 14th, but not the 12th.
Say that again for the record.
We can hold the 14th, but not the 12th. The 12th is not achievable.
Thank you. That is what I will tell my board.
And we will put it in writing today.
Before five, please. Their board meets at six.
Before five. Understood.
I'll update the schedule and tell the crew.
I'll hold the vans until Friday noon.
One open question: does the 14th include the training session, or is that a separate visit?
Installation on the 14th. Training is separate until we confirm the trainer.
Then I need that in the written note, with the change-order caveat.
I'll phrase it as: training date to be confirmed, commercial terms unchanged.
Good.
If training is separate, I need one more van on the 17th.
I'll confirm the van today.
Okay, we're done. Thanks everyone — I'll circulate the confirmation within the hour.
Thanks. Bye.
Bye.

meetings.summary: Kickoff for the Northgate fit-out. Handover targeted for the 12th, access survey due 16 October, training kept separate. A survey slip triggers a date review.

utterances.text: Welcome, everyone. This is the Northgate fit-out kickoff. Recording for the project record.
Thanks. I'll represent the client side.
I'll run through the plan, then we can challenge the dates.
I have the install plan open.
The working assumption is a handover in the week of the 12th.
The 12th is a board commitment. It needs to be real, not aspirational.
The crew can be on site from the 8th if access is ready.
Access is the thing I cannot promise until the survey is done.
Then the survey is the first milestone.
Who owns the access survey?
My facilities lead, but I need your checklist.
I'll send the checklist today.
Target the 12th for handover, with the survey complete by the 16th of October.
The 16th is tight but possible.
Let's write both dates down: survey by the 16th, handover on the 12th.
Agreed.
I need to know whether the loading bay is available on Saturdays.
It normally is, but I will confirm.
That could matter if the date moves.
Let's not plan around a move yet.
I'd rather plan around reality.
Fair. The 12th is the earliest we can commit. Anything earlier is not honest.
Then we commit to the 12th and protect it.
And if the survey slips, we revisit immediately.
Agreed. Survey slip is a trigger for a date review.
Anything else before we close?
Training is still quoted separately. Keep it separate for now.
Noted. Training separate.
I'll circulate the plan and the trigger.
Thank you. Bye.
